newsitem.title: USA: US Commerce's Ehrlich sees Q4 spending rising - RFTV.
newsitem.headline: US Commerce's Ehrlich sees Q4 spending rising - RFTV.

text.p: Consumer spending will come back in the fourth quarter, U.S. Commerce Department Undersecretary for Economics Everett Ehrlich said Wednesday.

"The consumer's going to come back. (He) caught his breath in the third quarter, increased the savings rate by a percentage point, (it's) very unlikely we'll see another one point increase in (Q4). ... Employment is growing, income is high, consumer confidence is at very high levels. You can see the consumer coming back. I think there's every reason to believe retailers who believe we're going to see a strong Christmas season," he told Reuters Financial Television.

"I think we see continued growth in profits and that means ongoing strong investment. We had a very strong quarter for investment in the third quarter. The prospect is for more of the same in the fourth," he said, adding that he foresaw goverment spending rising in the fourth quarter also.

Most of the third-quarter business inventory build was "warranted and wanted" to compensate for de-stocking over the past 18 months, and although Q4 inventory build may not match that of Q3 but "we should see an inventory build," he added.

"All told I think the fourth quarter is going to have a higher rate of growth than the third," he said, soon after news that Q3 U.S. Gross Domestic Product grew at 2.2 percent after Q2's 4.7 percent rate.

Expected export growth will come from the fact that the economies of major trading partners such as Japan, Europe, Canada and Mexico had "bottomed out," Ehrlich said, adding he did not see another large increase in the trade deficit in Q4.
He saw more room for wage rises paid for out of higher productivity, adding "The economy's in a groove: We have sustainable growth, we have strong investment, ... we have inflation under control."
